description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

Our Brand Marketing team at Plaid builds awareness, shapes perception, and grows Plaid's presence in the market. We combine deep product and industry knowledge with strong creative instincts. We want Plaid known and trusted by the companies and people who rely on financial technology. We believe every company offering financial products to consumers deserves the best financial technology, and people should understand why it matters.

As our Social Community Manager, you'll help us get there. You'll build and run Plaid's social communities, showing up where our audience already is, listening closely, and turning those conversations into trust. You'll also help bring customer and employee voices to the forefront, so the people who know Plaid best are the ones telling its story.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Managing day-to-day engagement across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, and Reddit, responding to comments, DMs, and mentions with a voice that's human first

- Proactively building community, customer love, and advocacy - identifying and nurturing fans, developers, and customers into repeat advocates for Plaid (superfans, referrals, UGC)

- Defining Plaid's voice on social media, in partnership with the Social Lead and larger Brand team

- Staying culturally tuned in, knowing what trend or moment is worth jumping on and what to skip

- Monitoring conversations and sentiment across channels, flagging trends, questions, or risks to the Social Lead and relevant teams

- Supporting execution of community-facing content and campaigns in partnership with content and design

- Adapting tone and approach for each platform's distinct culture and norms

- Tracking engagement metrics and contributing to regular reporting

- Escalating sensitive situations, including PR risk or customer issues, quickly and calmly

QUALIFICATIONS

- 3-5 years of experience managing B2B social channels, in-house, including building community and customer advocacy

- Working knowledge of LinkedIn, X, Instagram, YouTube, and Reddit, including the distinct culture and etiquette of each platform

- A sharp, current feel for internet/meme culture and what's culturally relevant right now

- Strong, adaptable writing skills, with the ability to shift tone across channels while staying on-brand

- A level head under pressure, with good judgment on when to respond directly versus escalate

- Interest in fintech or technology, with a genuine curiosity to learn the space

- Strong organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple platforms and stakeholders at once

Our mission at Plaid is to unlock financial freedom for everyone. To support that mission, we seek to build a diverse team of driven individuals who care deeply about making the financial ecosystem more equitable. We recognize that strong qualifications can come from both prior work experiences and lived experiences. We encourage you to apply to a role even if your experience doesn't fully match the job description. We are always looking for team members that will bring something unique to Plaid!

Our customers run their busiest weeks of the year on HubSync , and our test pipeline has to be something they can count on: when a pipeline is red, it means something real; when it is green, the team trusts it enough to ship.
Our test framework is AI-assisted by design. Engineers define what a test should check, Claude Code writes the test code under versioned skill-file rules, and a convention linter plus tiered CI gates (PR, deploy, and nightly) hold the standard. The architecture is settled. This person will own it, extend it, and help the rest of engineering use it well. Key Responsibilities
Gate & Signal Ownership

• Triage CI failures to root cause, so every gate failure gets a real disposition instead of a re-run.

• Run test quarantine with discipline: flaky tests go in with a tracking ticket and an owner, and come back out fixed or deleted.

• Lead the quarterly review of the PR gate so only tests that earn their place stay in it.

• Protect signal quality over green builds; a gate that passes because tests were skipped or deleted is a failed gate.

Framework Engineering

• Own and extend the shared test framework: fixtures, factories, the API client, page object conventions, and CI test mapping.

• Lead the move of the convention linter from shell-based checks to AST-aware tooling.

• Build reusable patterns for hard problems, such as complex grid assertions and external signing ceremonies, so feature teams don't have to solve them again.

• Own the skills system that governs AI-written tests; design the rules that define what the model may write and what it must refuse.

• Trace violations in AI-written tests back to their source and fix them in the skill files, not in review comments.

• Re-validate those rules whenever the underlying model changes.

• Review generated tests for convention compliance and real test value.

• Help developers adopt the workflow: pair on their first tests, turn recurring friction into framework fixes or skill updates, and keep the path from test idea to merged, passing test short.

Direct Test Authoring

• Write tests, page objects, and fixtures directly where the stakes or the difficulty call for it: critical-path coverage, reference implementations that set the pattern, and problems too complex to delegate.

• Proven experience building or owning a test framework, not just writing tests inside one.

• Hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, including being the person accountable when the build broke.

• Deep TypeScript expertise; Playwright strongly preferred.

• Strong review judgment: the ability to look at a passing test and tell whether it verifies anything.

• Genuine interest in AI-assisted development and the governance questions that come with it.
